tasks.spec:
You are an engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the freytag-forge repository (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch any other checkout, never run `uv`, NEVER call a model (not `claude`, not `codex`), NEVER use the network, never run `python -m bench run`, never write factory/state/. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv . Environment for every command: `export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp`. Ruff (python files only): `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` / `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` (line length 120, Python 3.12). Never pass --cov to pytest. Run tests as `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 <files>`. Tests must be hermetic (no network, no real model). Shared code must stay story-agnostic (no story, scene or character names in production code; tests may use the repository's real story package and must also cover a synthetic package). ARCHITECTURE RULE (AGENTS.md, firm): world-model logic, meaning anything that reads or changes only world state, is a `World` method in packages/worldkeeper with its tests in packages/worldkeeper/tests; `storygame` only adapts and calls it. If an OLD test pins behaviour this change deliberately changes, update it and say so in NOTES.txt. Write NOTES.txt (worktree root, never committed) listing every ambiguity and your choice. Read first: AGENTS.md, docs/contributor-guide.md, docs/world-model-grounding.md. BACKGROUND. Scenes can now be entered without playing the preceding scenes (hosted `start_scene`, see storygame/runtime/entry_seed.py). Measured: `bare` entry (scene entry fact and placements only) leaves about 110 story facts unset and every earned item hidden at scene 3B; `thorough` entry (a persona that earns everything optional) is path-dependent and also not a state a real player has. The fix is a canonical, versioned entry state per scene: the world after a deterministic player earns only what the route requires. 

You may edit or create ONLY: packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py, packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/state_export.py (new), packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/__init__.py, packages/worldkeeper/tests/test_state_export.py (new).

TASK. Give `World` a way to export its world-only state, load it back, and check entry invariants. All three are `World` methods (implementation may live in the new module and be called from thin methods):
1. `World.export_state() -> dict`: deterministic, JSON-safe, sorted, covering EVERY `wk_*` fact the world keeps (parent, relation, hidden, axis, name, alias, owner, companion, moved, condition, unplaced, status, place text, kind, fixed, seeded and any other `wk_` predicate used in model.py or incidental.py). Shape: {"schema": 1, "facts": [{"predicate", "subject", "object", "value"}, ...]} sorted by (predicate, subject, object, value). The FactBackend protocol has no enumeration method, so enumerate by an explicit module-level tuple `WORLD_PREDICATES` of every wk_ predicate. Add a drift test: build a World on a MemoryBackend, run representative operations (seed, place, move, take or hold, hide/reveal, set an axis, add an alias, companion, anything else the public API offers), then assert that every `wk_*` fact in the backend (`MemoryBackend.matching_all`) appears in the export, so a future wk_ predicate that is not listed fails the test.
2. `World.import_state(state: dict) -> OpResult`: replaces the world's `wk_*` facts with the snapshot's. It refuses (OpResult(False, reason), changing nothing) a snapshot with an unknown schema number, an unknown predicate, or a subject entity the schema does not declare. Import then export round-trips to an identical dict (test it, including importing into a World that already had other state).
3. `World.entry_problems(protagonist_id, location_id) -> tuple[str, ...]`: plain-words invariant violations, empty when sound. Check: every entity that has a parent has exactly one `wk_parent` and the parent exists; no parent cycle; the protagonist exists and its area chain contains `location_id`; no item held by the protagonist (directly or through its container chain) is still marked hidden; every `wk_axis` value is one of the axis's declared poles; every companion subject and object exists. Use the real accessors (`chain`, `holder`, `holds`, `axis_definitions`, `exists`) rather than re-deriving.
4. A pure function `diff_states(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict` in state_export.py with keys `added`, `removed`, `changed` (facts keyed by predicate and subject) for readable review output; export it from `worldkeeper/__init__.py`.

TESTS (packages/worldkeeper/tests/test_state_export.py, hermetic, whole file under 10 s): build schemas the way the existing tests in that folder do (study test_holds.py and test_can_represent.py). Cover the drift test, round trip, refusals (each of the three), each invariant (a passing and a failing case each), deterministic ordering (two worlds built in different operation orders but equal state export identically), and diff_states. Do not assert exact message strings beyond that the right entity id appears. Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider packages/worldkeeper/tests tests/test_world_model.py`.
tasks.check:
set -eo pipefail
WORK=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-23
mkdir -p "$WORK/out"
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
git add -A -- storygame bench tests packages docs
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vE '^(packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model\.py|packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/state_export\.py|packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/__init__\.py|packages/worldkeeper/tests/test_state_export\.py)$' || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
start=$(date +%s)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 packages/worldkeeper/tests tests/test_world_model.py
grep -q 'def export_state' packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py || { echo 'World.export_state missing'; exit 1; }
grep -q 'def import_state' packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py || { echo 'World.import_state missing'; exit 1; }
grep -q 'def entry_problems' packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py || { echo 'World.entry_problems missing'; exit 1; }
grep -q 'WORLD_PREDICATES' packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/state_export.py || { echo 'WORLD_PREDICATES missing'; exit 1; }
took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))
echo "checks took $took s (budget 300 s)"
[ "$took" -le 300 ] || { echo "over the 300 s budget"; exit 1; }
PYFILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep '\.py$' || true)
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff check $PYFILES
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check $PYFILES
git diff --cached > "$WORK/out/worldkeeper-state-export.patch"
test -s "$WORK/out/worldkeeper-state-export.patch"
tasks.verified: World exports, imports and checks its world-only state; a drift test catches any unlisted wk_ predicate.

TASK. Add a deterministic CANONICAL path: a player who earns only what the route requires, so the state at each scene's entry is the story's own minimum, not a thorough sweep. Read storygame/personas.py (`_select_thorough`, `_run`, `PERSONAS`, `run_persona`), storygame/story_package/obligations.py (`required_storylet_ids`: the storylets the route events and bridge events need, with prerequisites), storygame/runtime/entry_seed.py and tests/test_persona_escalation.py first.
1. In personas.py add persona `canonical` (a short plain description like the others) and `_select_canonical(package, state, candidates)`: among candidates that survive the turn (`_candidate_survives_turn`), choose only those whose storylet is in `required_storylet_ids(package)`, ranked exactly as `_select_thorough` ranks (bridge-missing facts first, then id) restricted to that set; when none qualifies return None (the player waits, so pacing and bridge events advance). Wire it into `_run` the way thorough and wrong_lead are wired, without changing their behaviour. No story, scene or fact names in the code.
2. In entry_seed.py give `advance_state_to_scene(package, state, scene_id, persona='thorough')` a `persona` parameter (default keeps today's behaviour; the selector is chosen by name, `thorough` or `canonical`; any other name raises ValueError) and add `canonical_path_report(package) -> list[dict]`: starting from `RuntimeState.bootstrap(package)`, advance scene by scene with the canonical persona and return one row per hop `{from_scene, to_scene, turns, earned, transition_cause, storylets_delivered}` where `earned` is true only when the engine records an earned transition (read how the runtime records the transition cause and the persona report's `turns_to_exit`; a transition forced by the handoff timer is NOT earned). The report must never raise just because a hop was forced: it records it. If the canonical player cannot reach a scene at all within `_turn_cap`, the row says `reached: false` instead of raising.

TESTS (new tests/test_canonical_entry_path.py, hermetic, whole file under 40 s): (a) canonical path reaches every scene of the repository's real story package in order; (b) it is deterministic: two runs give identical `state.facts` (compare the sorted tuples of every asserted fact) at every scene entry; (c) the canonical state at each scene is a subset, by true story facts, of the thorough state at the same scene (`canonical <= thorough` on true non-wk facts) and strictly smaller for at least one scene; (d) `canonical_path_report` returns one row per hop with the keys above; (e) an unknown persona name raises ValueError; (f) `thorough` behaviour is unchanged (an existing persona test still passes, and the default call equals the old result). IMPORTANT: do not hide a failure. Whatever the real earned/forced result is for each hop, assert only the report's SHAPE and write the real per-hop table into NOTES.txt (scene, turns, earned, cause) so a reviewer can read it. Add the test file to tests/shard_durations.json with `.venv/bin/python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only` (never `uv`; by hand with a measured duration rounded up if that needs network). Run tests/test_canonical_entry_path.py tests/test_persona_escalation.py tests/test_start_scene_session.py and the bench seeding tests (`ls tests/test_bench*.py`).
